29. **Lineage is queryable at the minimum.** What created the objective (agent-created or hand-created). The path that agent took from that creation to completion. The completion event. Time it took. Map it correctly. That is querying, not a new module. If it is not queryable, the loop is not real.
30. **Campaign failure is an event.** Global and local apply (all campaign failures vs **this** campaign). Then an **in-app action**: create a record — even as simple as **ascribe a tag**. Named example: the subscription bell (subscribed / not) **is a tag** created in Automations. Opt-out / unsubscribe is also an event; it assigns that tag. Campaign fails → ascribes that tag. This is one of the first in-app actions named. Do not invent the rest of the action catalog.

On the Agents action there are two choices: **assign to an existing sequence**, or **create from a template**. No third choice: author a new agent here. Can evolve later — not now. Plate **A14**. A8 stays prior for select-agent = whole sequence. A12 stays the form. The sequence pick (Opt-in / Re-engagement / Reactivation) is a **radio**. Teaching walk: **firm created / provisioned** → **audit the contacts** → **if X** (condition node, previous result) → **agents**. ## After an action: the previous result is every write that run made

That is the primitive. It applies to every action. We do not specify a field list.

The action **passes the work to the real module**. When that module finishes, **every write that run made** is available to the next node. The next node **picks** which of those writes it is about.

Audit produces a lot of writes (the run, verdicts, sequence-ready, whatever else that run touched). All of that is available. Provision, given the form values, runs — every write from **that** run is available. Same shape.

“Two things” on Audit was a bad restatement. Two grains showed up because that module writes a batch row **and** per-person rows. That is the write-set. It is not a law that every action has two outputs.

**How you pick:** point the If at a write (or a field of a write) already on that handle. A person-row write splits people. A run-row write is the artifact.

**Not the previous result:** hearing the completion as a **trigger** on a different automation. That is the other door.

Hub `lastOutput` → `lastInput` is the smell, not the live path. Live is SA **015** (engineer). Do not recut it here.

## Shape: when a node finishes, you have what the module produced

This is the whole question. Automations only works if this is true.

An action is not a fake step. It **sends the work to the real module** (Audit, Contacts, Agents — whatever that action is). That module does its job, same as if you had pressed it on that desk.

When that node **completes**, the next step has **everything that module produced** — every write, every result — **as if you had done it in the module.** Naturally. Not a special automation-only copy. Not a guess.

Example: Audit action.

1. The node hands Audit **who we are auditing**.
2. Audit runs. It writes whatever that module writes.
3. After the node, **every write from that run** is the previous result. The next node picks. Not a short list we specified.

Same for Provision: this form submitted → pass the values → every write from that provision run.

### Two layers. That is the whole shape.

| Layer | What it is |
|-------|------------|
| **The writes** | Live in the module. **Every write that run made.** Same records you would open on that desk. Not a shadow copy Automations invented. |
| **The handle** | After this node, the next step is pointing at **those** writes — not “go find some audit.” The next node **picks** which write. |

A wire that looks like an n8n **pipe** is one way to see the handle. A then-this list where the next node reads **this node’s output id** is the same product. **Pipe vs this-then-that is not the question.** The question is: when the node completes, do we have the module’s output. If the next step has to guess (latest audit for this firm), it is not this node.

“Everything it produces” means **every write that run made**. Not a short list. Not the entire database from other runs. The If is calling from **that**.

| Door | What it is |

## The law

**Records that show inside a module come from tables.** A reasonable count of rows in the requisite tables — not a thick fake world, not an empty module.

**Never hard-code data into the app.** Not in a React table. Not in a painted empty-state that pretends there are people. Not a name, a tag, a verdict, a run, a firm, a contact baked into the component so the screen looks full.

When we **mint** a table or a field (and as we go, where that mint is already stood up): **populate the seed** (`supabase/seeds/`) so the module that reads it has records. The desk shows what the query returns.

---

## If the table or field is missing

Chrome can be specified. PM specifies the face. That is not a store.

If the **table** is missing, or the **field** is missing, or it is unspecified what to write — that is a **Systems Analyst** problem. Name it. **Do not build** until SA has ascribed what the row is, so you know what to do.

Do not invent the table in the SPA to finish the plate. Do not fill the plate with hard-coded rows while you wait.

### 7. Engagement / sequencing

Two engines that must **never** be conflated (`Seed §5.5`; `World §3.3`). The engagement **record** (Activity / chart) is a chronology of events that already fired — it authors nothing (`Seed §5.5`; `World §3.2`).

#### Shared phase law

**The system must be able to:**

- Run phases: **Opt-in** → **Re-engagement (nudges)** → **Reactivation** (`Seed §5.3`; `World §0.4`).
- Hold reactivation as **armed** (ghost template ready, nothing sending) vs **active** (executing) (`Seed §5.3`; `World §0.4`).
- Author sequences as ordered steps of channel + copy; treat reactivation/launch agents as composites of those steps; enroll when criteria match (`Seed §5.5`).
- Keep composing = configuration; sending = automation/Wiring (`Seed §5.5`; `World §1.3`).

#### 7a. Campaign calendar (content order across days)

**Must fulfill:** Decide day-ordered engagement content for a phase, under Engine 2 precedence.

**The system must be able to:**

- Hold opt-in / nudge / reactivation **content order** across days (`Seed §5.5`; `World §0.4, §3.3`).
- Obey Engine 2 precedence when choosing which motion's content runs (`World §3.3`).

**Must not:** Decide runtime channel ownership, waits, or attempt retries (that is 7b) (`World §3.3`).

#### 7b. Attempt / channel-ownership engine (one sequence at runtime)

**Must fulfill:** Run a single in-flight sequence under one owning channel, forward-only, with faceless criteria and inbound override.

**The system must be able to:**

- Own the flow under one channel at a time along **Text → Email → Form** (forward-only handoff) (`Seed §5.5`; `World §3.3`).
- Nest waits / attempts under the owning channel that failed; escalate forward when **criteria are met** (`Seed §5.5`; `World §0.4, §3.3`).
- Accept a **live inbound** mid-attempt as an override that can nullify the in-flight attempt (`World §0.4, §3.3`).
- On a **finishing event**, close the sequence and **arm the next** (`World §3.3`).
- Record every fired event on the engagement record without letting the record author motion (`Seed §5.5`; `World §3.2`).

**OPERATOR-REVISIONS clarifiers (not Seed/World law until promoted)** — denser prototype criteria in [`OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md`](./OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md) §5b:

- Text delivered not opened in **30 min** → Email.
- Email opened, link not clicked in **24 h** → next attempt.
- Form started not submitted in **24 h** → Text; re-entries do not reset the clock.
- Attempts are **local retries** under the failed owner (fresh Text→Email→Form), not a top-level Attempt spanning all channels.
- Live **form visit** is a named inbound override that can open the next step.
- Form submitted closes the nudge and can arm the next (e.g. reactivation scheduled).

**OPERATOR-REVISIONS clarifier — goal / class-as-objective (not Seed/World law until promoted).** Founder expansion 2026-08-15, durable: a **goal is a completion of an objective**; sequence **classes are classes of objective** (opt-in, re-engagement = data request, reactivation = meeting request); mini-goals are checkmarks **inside** a class; escalation already has several levels (attempt sequencing · mini-goals · sequence completion · **between campaigns**); **goals as escalation events** is the level that emerges. Reactivation’s completion **is** meeting booked — do not call that “no goal.” Full excerpts + housing vs gap: [`SYSTEMS-GOAL.md`](./SYSTEMS-GOAL.md). Do not extract Requirements or mint a table from that file until this block is promoted into a Story **must**.

**Must not:**

- Let Engine 2 replace the attempt engine inside a sequence (`World §0.4`).
- Let the engagement record author channel order or attempts (`World §3.2`).

**Chains to:** Each touchpoint carries Fact-refresh data asks; finishing events arm the next sequence; chosen motions arrive from Engine 2 (`Seed §5.4, §5.8`; `World §3.3`).

**Silences:** Exact product-locked criteria windows (beyond World’s “when criteria are met”); SMS reply-failure escalation (`Seed §13.15`); event-based enrollment trigger set beyond manual pull (`Seed §5.6, §11`). Goal-as-required-completion / goals-as-escalation-events is **not** a silence to fill from Requirements — it is a founder expansion parked in [`SYSTEMS-GOAL.md`](./SYSTEMS-GOAL.md) until promoted.

---

### 8. Fact-refresh / data-collection

**Must fulfill:** Use touchpoints as the data-collection mechanism; route answers by field class; write back into eligibility.

**The system must be able to:**

- Fire nudges that ask for or infer facts affecting eligibility (`Seed §5.4`; `World §0.4`).
- Classify fields and route:
  - **Self-reportable** → forms / pre-meeting capture.
  - **Document-dependent** → **never** a form; tracked work items.
  - **Employer-directed** → ask the **firm**, not the client (`Seed §5.4`; `World §0.4`).
- Accept answers from the client or consultant hand-entry; on any write-back, initiate **immediate re-evaluation** (`Seed §5.8`).
- Record a *missing* fact as a signal (Engine 2 input) (`Seed §5.8`).

**Must not:** Put document-dependent needs into forms (`Seed §5.4`).

**Chains to:** Every write-back triggers Eligibility; missing facts feed Engine 2 (`Seed §5.8`).

**Silences:** Client desk depth (touchpoint-only vs authenticated portal) (`Seed §13.4`); D-02 in-meeting fallback surface (`Seed §5.8, §13.5`).

---

### 9. Reference-currency

**Must fulfill:** Keep IRCC-shaped reference facts current as versioned data, with no code deploy.

**The system must be able to:**

- Maintain versioned reference tables (categories, trades, cutoffs, provincial identifiers, etc.) as **data** (`Seed §5.7`; `World §1.3, §2.2.1`).
- Treat a reference move (draw threshold/cutoff shift, category added, trade/provincial identifier change) as a **faceless** first-class trigger — no screen, no human click (`Seed §5.7`; `World §2.2.1`).
- Hold industry criteria packs (Constants) as versioned packs; V1 truth is Canada-shaped (`Seed §5.6, §2.6`).

**Must not:** Require a code deploy to update reference facts (`Seed §5.7` Directive 3).

**Chains to:** A reference change triggers Eligibility re-evaluation for every affected contact — the **law / public-reference** side of detection (`World §2.2`).

**Silences:** Ownership / IP / liability of rule packs (`Seed §13.9`; `World §1.2`); Constants packs beyond Immigration (`Seed §13.16`).

---

### 10. Eligibility re-evaluation

**Must fulfill:** Recompute private service eligibility when client facts or reference move; emit every determination as a signal.

**The system must be able to:**

- Evaluate from firm-held + engagement-collected client facts against house-held / firm-configured rules — **private** to the firm book (`Seed §2.4`; `World §0.4`).
- Accept two detection sides: (1) law/public-reference moves, (2) life-change facts only the person/firm-file knows (`World §2.2`).
- Run the automation shape: Trigger (scoped pull — manual rich; event thinner) → Constants → Conditions → Rules → structured output → downstream resolution (`Seed §5.6`; `World §0.4, §2.3`).
- Treat pathway pass as **any** pathway assertion (CEC **or** FSW **or** FST **or** PNP-*), not one favoured pathway (`Seed §5.7` Directive 2; `World §0.4`).
- Produce an **Analysis** readout (headlines, deltas, service candidates, nudge/reactivation hints) with machine output retained underneath (`Seed §5.7`; `World §0.4`).
- Emit **every** determination — including missing-data — as a signal (`Seed §5.8`).
- Keep evaluation inspectable/changeable without deploy (open-box / house layer) (`World §3.4, §2.1`).

**Must not:**

- Cold-detect strangers’ immigration eligibility from public databases as Core Function (`Seed §2.4, §14`; `World §0.4`).
- Treat a static book dump as sufficient for the life-change side (`World §2.2`).

**Chains to:** Every emitted signal triggers Engine 2 (`Seed §5.8`).

**Silences:** Operations & Actions initiation law (stubs) (`Seed §5.6, §11`); event-trigger set (`Seed §5.6, §11`); Rules UI toggles vs condition trees (`Seed §13.13`); workflow persistence target (`Seed §13.12`).

---

### 11. Signal / motion orchestration (Engine 2)

**Must fulfill:** Record every detection; choose the single outbound motion by fixed precedence.

**The system must be able to:**

- Record every detection — including missing data — as a **signal** when found (`Seed §5.8`; `World §0.4`).
- Decide outreach separately from recording, under fixed precedence (`Seed §5.8`):
  1. **Reactivation first**, whenever anything is reactivation-worthy.
  2. **Nudge only** when nothing is reactivation-worthy.
  3. When a nudge fires, consolidate **every** outstanding self-reportable need into **one** form — never one nudge per field.
  4. When reactivation fires, attach secondary signals as **agenda** on the consultant’s pre-meeting brief — never parallel outreach.
  5. **One client, one motion, ever** (`Seed §5.8, §16.11`; `World §3.3`).

**Must not:** Replace the attempt engine inside a sequence (`World §0.4`); fire parallel motions for one client (`Seed §5.8`).

**Chains to:** Chosen motion hands work to Engagement (reactivation or nudge sequence) (`Seed §5.8`; `World §3.3`).

**Silences:** What makes a signal **reactivation-worthy** (`Seed §5.8`); D-01 / D-02 builder placement (`Seed §5.8, §13.5`).

---

### 12. Meeting / loop-closer

**Must fulfill:** On meeting booked, close the loop with pending capture and a live brief.

**The system must be able to:**

- Treat **meeting booked** as the core success / loop-closer event (`Seed §4, §5.8`).
- On `meeting_booked` with outstanding self-reportable fields, open a data-capture form pending the meeting (`Seed §5.8`; `World §0.4`).
- On any write-back against that capture (or consultant entry), run **immediate re-evaluation** (`Seed §5.8`).
- Keep the pre-meeting brief **live** (recomputed), not a snapshot (`Seed §5.8`; `World §0.4`).

**Chains to:** Write-backs re-trigger Eligibility, keeping the brief current (`Seed §5.8`).

**Silences:** D-01 — pre-meeting capture as tail of reactivation vs standalone `meeting_booked` sequence; D-02 — in-meeting fallback module (`Seed §5.8, §13.5`).

# Decision constitution — bottlenecks hide in catch-all buckets

**Parent doctrine:** [`../sme/DOCTRINE-sme-cto-implementation.md`](../sme/DOCTRINE-sme-cto-implementation.md) §8  
**Scope:** Om Coda operating constraint — portable across products, not Tower-only  
**Status:** Standing method

---

## Principle

Any category that looks like a decision but is really an un-examined deferral is where work and bottlenecks disappear.

> **"The CTO handles it"** and **"let the founder review it"** are the *same failure* at different layers.

The fix is identical: name the classes explicitly, and let no bucket be the place where un-adjudicated work goes to vanish.

---

## Origin

Two instances converged in the same Tower conversation:

1. **Capability vanishing into the CTO sink** — deliverability filed as "just wiring," never becoming a consideration ([doctrine §2](../sme/DOCTRINE-sme-cto-implementation.md)).
2. **Founder throughput becoming the company's bottleneck** — progress waiting on presence rather than on named decisions.

Both dissolve the same way — by enumerating decision/work classes ahead of time so the default is autonomous and only *named* classes interrupt a human.

---

## Mechanics

For every catch-all ("CTO handles it," "founder reviews it," "TBD later"), demand the split:

1. What specifically is in here?  
2. Which items need a **named owner / named gate** vs proceed on method?

**Working example — Register fail-closed markers:**

- `NEEDS VERIFICATION`
- `BLOCKED (counsel)`
- Persona / World seat changes need room sign-off

The pass proceeds autonomously and stops only at named gates.

**Applied to the founder:** path to *progress depending on decisions, not presence* — a small, pre-enumerated founder-only decision class; everything else method-adjudicated. Portable across every Om Coda product from inception.

---

## Suggested founder-only class (seed — product may refine)

Keep this list short; expand only with room sign-off:

- World / persona seat minting or retirement  
- Hard-stop / never-invent doctrine changes  
- Money-door / escrow release unit changes that alter the commercial bet  
- Geography / regulatory regime expansion that reopens SME seats  
- Explicit `BLOCKED (counsel)` adjudication

Everything else: method + specialist + builder columns.

# Tower — Seed (dense provision)

**Product:** Tower  
**Company:** Om Coda  
**Audience / buyer:** Immigration consultancies (B2B firm operators)  
**As of:** 2026-07-27  
**Status:** Validated 2026-07-27 — World derived in `WORLD.md`  

**Law of Seed:** Everything we know, every assumption, every bet — product *and* how they get in. Under-provisioning Seed is the primary cause of thin Worlds — ecosystems that look complete on the page but lack enough density for seats, admission, and outcomes to stay honest. World is *derived* from this dump by a world-builder BA; agents must not invent business facts outside it.

**Related sources folded in (Seed wins on conflict):** `docs/ideas/tower-product-vision.md`, `docs/ideas/audit-module.md`, `docs/product/psd/tower/PSD-tower-v0.4.0.md`, `docs/product/immigration-rules-engine2-giveback.md`, `docs/product/auth-service-contract.md`, `docs/product/database-seeding-protocol.md`, How graphs (`consultantOnTower`, `towerCoreOutcome`), ALG acquisition/activation conversation (2026-07), operator shape bets in [`OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md`](./OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md), channel methodology first pass in `guidelines/Reactivation.md`.

---

## 0. The bets we’re making (read first)

### 0.1 Product bet (why Tower exists)

**We are betting that immigration firms will pay for an always-on system that engages their dormant and active contacts, keeps immigration facts fresh through firm→client touchpoints, re-evaluates service eligibility as IRCC-shaped rules and client facts move, and surfaces when someone is campaign-worthy — so consultants book meetings without manually rechecking every file.**

Tower is **not** a reactive CRM (“what do I do when someone emails?”). It is **proactive eligibility wrapped in engagement**.

**One-line value:** Give us your contacts; we engage them, keep their immigration picture current, and surface when eligibility changes — without manually rechecking every file.

### 0.2 Growth bet (how firms get in — ALG)

**ALG** = agent-led growth: cheap acquire + get to proof without a sales call as the primary door and without making the stranger self-serve through a long onboarding form. (Defined fully in §6.)

**We are betting that immigration consultancies will convert into *running* Tower clients through ALG — not through sales calls as the primary door and not through self-serve onboarding forms — if one tap in a Meta feed makes a prepared campaign workspace legible, cheap public seed inputs provision that workspace, and an agent earns the hard inputs (database authorization + escrow) before the campaign actually runs.**

Compressed growth bets:

1. **Acquisition:** Consultant scrolling Meta (FB/IG) gives name + website + phone/email within a **click budget** if they understand what one tap yields — without persuasion theater. Pull, not push. “Email enters on evidence, not on ideas.”
2. **Activation:** From those seed inputs alone, automation **forward-deploys** a no-login prepared workspace (Om Coda launch → re-engagement → reactivation methodology staged under their firm identity) and an agent walks them until they authorize DB access and accept **escrow** — then the campaign can **run**.
3. **Application retention:** Once running, the always-on desk loop (below) is what retains and justifies ongoing money — **without reshaping the application desk** for the acquisition experiment.
4. **Anti-bets:** Cold email is not V1 on ideas. Credits and sales-call are not peer doors at activation. Public-before-contact detection of *end-client* eligibility is not Tower. **Agent is never fulfillment** — the chat/voice surface does not *do* the work (it does not scrape the firm site, instantiate campaign templates, fire sequences, evaluate rules, send OTP, or move money). Those jobs belong to Automations and Wiring; the agent only presents, asks, and routes the human toward them.

If the growth bet is wrong, we learn it cheaply on ads and a planted click-through of the feed→capture journey — not by rebuilding the product first.

### 0.3 Contingent-cost bet (Om Coda money posture)

Across Om Coda products we prefer **contingent cost**: the buyer’s cost is zero (or held) until outcome terms are met. For Tower ALG activation, the presented door is **escrow**, not prepaid credits. Ongoing SaaS packaging may still exist later — it must not replace escrow as a peer door at the activation payment moment.

### 0.4 Agent bet

**Agent = presentation only** (request / respond / route). Picture the split:

| Agent does (presentation) | Not agent — Automations / Wiring |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Asks for name, website, phone/email on Approach | Persists the capture and attributes the session |
| Explains what the prepared workspace already shows | Forward-deploys the workspace; scrapes public firm facts; instantiates Om Coda methodology templates |
| Asks the consultant to authorize DB access / accept escrow | Stores the authorization; holds escrow; flips campaign to **running** |
| Points at “arm this audit” / “send this sequence” in Hub | Runs the audit pull, enrolls contacts, fires messages on schedule |
| Answers “why is this person eligible?” by routing to Analysis | Evaluates immigration rules against Client Data |

Never label Automations runtime or Auth Service as “the agent doing work.”

---

## 1. What Seed is (and is not)

| Seed is | Seed is not |
|---------|-------------|
| Bets, market, product mechanics, eligibility law, Hub modules, engagement philosophy, ALG lattice, money, gates, prototype honesty, assumptions, open decisions | Derived ecosystem (**World**) |
| Enough density that a BA can derive seats, admission, and facet outcomes without inventing the business | SME Pass1 answers or platform strategy from SMEs |
| Both **application truth** and **how strangers become running clients** | A funnel sketch or a feature backlog |

**Activation sets the target; acquisition fulfills the seed quota.** Application is the desk that performs once running. Evolution is product change from running feedback — named, lightly specified here.

---

## 2. Market & buyer

### 2.1 Who buys

Immigration consultancies / practices that hold or can obtain **contact lists** (past clients, leads, CRM exports, spreadsheets) and sell immigration services (pathway advice, applications, retainers). Primary operator: **consultant / firm operator** at the desk.

### 2.2 What they lose today

- Booked consults and retainer starts when eligible people sit dark in a list.

# Systems — change packet 022 (Objective met is a Local event)

**Seat:** Systems Analyst.
**When:** 2026-08-21 09:30 UTC.
**What this is:** the cut that makes **“this sequence ran, the objective is met”** the same mechanism as a Local trigger. Implementer **only implements**. No analysis left.
**Why:** Founder: events/triggers already have a solid mechanism underneath — a write we designated as a trigger. Objective met must have that same underneath. *“This specific form is filled and submitted by this user… back into the system, so the system can detect it and say: oh, they submitted this form — what’s that sequence?”* That mapping-and-matching is this packet.
**Join:** 010 housing (`campaign`, `campaign_objective`) · 017 `event_write_set` / `event_test_data` · A26 Local axes (`triggerLocalRefFromPayload` / `triggerLocalAxesMatch`) · [`PRIMITIVES.md`](./PRIMITIVES.md) row **“An objective was met”** · [`SYSTEMS-GOAL.md`](./SYSTEMS-GOAL.md) · flagship [`PHASE-TWO-LOG.md`](./PHASE-TWO-LOG.md) **15:43**.
**Flag:** 15:43 untouched. **Do not recut 015 / 019.** **#108 merged** (`018_collectible_fields.sql`). This is the next cut.
**UI:** none required. Founder: the UI that exists is all the UI this needs. This is backend.
**Instructions:** founder only.

---

## 1. The mechanism, stated once

A Local event today is **two** things, and Tower already has both:

1. A **write** we designated as a trigger (event = the INSERT — law 1).
2. An **instance axis on that row**, so “this one” is answerable — not just “one of these happened.”

`contact_import` is Local because `contact_records.import_batch_id` **is a column**. `campaign_failure` is Local because `campaign_failure.campaign_id` **is a column**. The matcher (`triggerLocalAxesMatch`) then tests only the axes the operator specified.

**Objective met is exactly that shape.** The completion write **is** the event. Nothing new is needed conceptually.

**And the axis comes from a binding.** When the operator picks the objective on the Automations Action, they are **binding** that objective to something concrete — the column is already called `action.payload_binding`. Authorship binds; the runtime carries that binding out on the wire (§2.1) so the return leg can be matched. The stamp is not new information — it is the binding, made physical. §2.6 decides what it binds to.

What is missing is only (2) — **the completion rows do not carry which campaign asked for them:**

| Objective kind | Completion write (010) | Instance axis on the row today | Local possible? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meeting` | `meeting_booked` | `enrollment_id` (no FK) | **Nearly** — enrollment, not objective |
| `form` | `fact_writebacks` | **none.** `form_ref` is passed in the dispatch payload and **never persisted** (`004` has no such column) | **No** |
| `click` | `messaging_events` → `outbound_messages` | **none.** No enrollment / campaign / attempt column anywhere on the send | **No** |

That is the entire gap. It is not philosophical and it is not a missing Story must. **Two of the three objective kinds cannot be matched back to the sequence that asked.**

And so the current met-check is Global-shaped where it must be Local-shaped:

```
campaignHousing.campaignObjectiveMet()
  → SELECT 1 FROM <completion_table> WHERE firm_id=$1 AND contact_id=$2 LIMIT 1
```

**Any** meeting this person ever booked, **any** fact they ever submitted, **any** message event at all satisfies **any** campaign objective. A meeting booked last quarter completes today’s launch window. That is the bug the founder is pointing at.

**The fix is two halves: stamp the ask, then match the answer.**

---

## 2. Hard decisions

### 2.1 Stamp the ask (outbound carries the objective)

When a sequence deploys outreach **in pursuit of an objective**, the objective rides on what goes out. This is what makes the return leg matchable.

```sql
-- Sends carry the pursuit.
ALTER TABLE outbound_messages
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS enrollment_id TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS campaign_id TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS campaign_objective_id TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS attempt_id TEXT;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS outbound_messages_objective_idx
  ON outbound_messages (campaign_objective_id, contact_id);

-- The form is per-objective. Persist the instance axis that the payload already carries.
ALTER TABLE fact_writebacks
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS form_ref TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS campaign_objective_id TEXT;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS fact_writebacks_objective_idx
  ON fact_writebacks (campaign_objective_id, contact_id);

-- Meeting already knows the enrollment. Name the objective too.
ALTER TABLE meeting_booked
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS campaign_objective_id TEXT;
```

No FK on these (TEXT tenancy, same posture as `meeting_booked.enrollment_id`; `campaign_objective` rows are firm-copied by `copySequence`). Nullable — a send outside a sequence (OTP, probe, house form) stamps nothing and is therefore never a completion.

## Checklist Purpose: "Unit Tests for English"

**CRITICAL CONCEPT**: Checklists are **UNIT TESTS FOR REQUIREMENTS WRITING** - they validate the quality, clarity, and completeness of requirements in a given domain.

**NOT for verification/testing**:

- ❌ NOT "Verify the button clicks correctly"
- ❌ NOT "Test error handling works"
- ❌ NOT "Confirm the API returns 200"
- ❌ NOT checking if code/implementation matches the spec

**FOR requirements quality validation**:

- ✅ "Are visual hierarchy requirements defined for all card types?" (completeness)
- ✅ "Is 'prominent display' quantified with specific sizing/positioning?" (clarity)
- ✅ "Are hover state requirements consistent across all interactive elements?" (consistency)
- ✅ "Are accessibility requirements defined for keyboard navigation?" (coverage)
- ✅ "Does the spec define what happens when logo image fails to load?" (edge cases)

**Metaphor**: If your spec is code written in English, the checklist is its unit test suite. You're testing whether the requirements are well-written, complete, unambiguous, and ready for implementation - NOT whether the implementation works.

**Ownership and checkbox lifecycle**:

- Custom checklists generated by this command are reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifacts.
- `[x]` means the reviewer determined the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
- `[x]` does NOT mean implementation work is complete.
- This command generates or appends checklist items; it MUST NOT mark generated items `[x]`.
- An agent may assist with evaluating items only when explicitly asked by the reviewer.
- `checklists/requirements.md` is a separate built-in spec-quality checklist maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`; do not treat that exception as applying to custom checklists generated here.

# Tower V1 — Outcomes (clean)

**Source of truth for Function / How decomposition.** Prior PM lattice rewritten; see correction notes below.

**Two rules this obeys:**

1. **No "As Tower."** Outcomes belong only to human entities — the reference side of the coin.
   Tower and its modules are what the leaves *require* (the build side). An outcome's subject is
   never the app.
2. **Engagement machinery is a requirement, not an outcome.** Opt-in, nudge, reactivation, refresh,
   re-evaluate, detect — none of these are anyone's outcome. They fall out at the **leaves** when the
   Consultant's "get clients booked without running any of it" and the Operator's "author / bind /
   oversee" outcomes decompose. They appear nowhere as an "As X, I can engage…" line.

**Subjects:** **Consultant** (the one acquired persona) · **Engagement contact** (referenced
participant) · **Operator** (the single house/agency human — one entity working many surfaces, not
many personas).

**Core:** reserved for the one product north-star — the Consultant's. Everything else is supply,
marked secondary. (Candidate co-core: Operator · Activation & forward-deploy, the ALG onramp — left
secondary here; promote it if you want two north-stars.)

**How trees:** [`how/`](./how/) — one MD tree per outcome, decomposed to leaves with click-path
solutioning. Index: [`how/00-INDEX.md`](./how/00-INDEX.md).

---

## Correction from the prior PM lattice (why this rewrite)

The consultant's inputs all live at **acquisition and activation** — hand over the book, authorize
access, accept escrow, and hold the license the outreach runs under. In the **application** layer
under ALG they initiate nothing and configure nothing — the engine runs. So the consultant's core
is not *"I engage"* — it is *"I hand over the book and authorize it, and meetings show up without me
running anything."*

Their verbs are **hand over · authorize · receive** (plus standing governance). Everything the old
sentence claimed as theirs — opt-in, nudge, reactivation, refresh, re-evaluate — is machinery; it
surfaces as **requirements at leaves**, attributed to **operator-side** modules — not pulled back
under the consultant workspace. That cross-attribution is correct; "fixing" it back under the
consultant is the error this rewrite caught.

Every house/per-tenancy subject is **"As Operator"** — one human, many surfaces — never "As House"
(a place, not an actor).

---

## A. Consultant (persona — firm desk)

**Core**
> As Consultant, I can hand my private book to Tower and authorize it to work under my license, and
> get eligible clients booked onto my calendar — without setting up, configuring, or running any of
> the engagement myself — so that an eligible contact arrives at a booked meeting already re-engaged
> and current.

> *Note — this is the fix. The consultant's verbs are **hand over · authorize · receive**. Their
> inputs live at acquisition and activation; in the application layer under ALG they initiate and
> configure nothing. The old "engage through opt-in → nudge → reactivation…" verbs were machinery
> wearing a consultant wrapper — they are now requirements that decompose out of this outcome, not
> an outcome. None of that configuration lives in the consultant's space, so none of it is theirs.*

**Governance — secondary**
> As Consultant, I can keep everything running under my license and halt anything I won't stand
> behind — so that the book is worked lawfully in my name.

**Access — secondary**
> As Consultant, I can sign in and land in my firm workspace to see what's being done in my name and
> take the meetings booked for me. *(so-that local/obvious — omitted)*

---

## B. Engagement contact (referenced participant — closes the loop)

Not a persona. These exist so the Consultant's so-that has somewhere to land and the loop closes
back onto the Consultant.

**Consent — secondary**
> As Engagement contact, I can receive a firm-branded consent request and agree or ignore before any
> deeper collection.

**Refresh facts — secondary**

# Consultant — Core

**Kind:** core (sole north-star)  
**Subject:** Consultant

**Statement**
> As Consultant, I can hand my private book to Tower and authorize it to work under my license, and
> get eligible clients booked onto my calendar — without setting up, configuring, or running any of
> the engagement myself — so that an eligible contact arrives at a booked meeting already re-engaged
> and current.

**Handoff flag:** This tree is deliberately short on the consultant desk. Engagement / eligibility
machinery falls out as **requirements** attributed to **operator** modules. Do not pull that
machinery back under Consultant.

---

## Root — outcome

**Clarity:** *(statement above)*  
**Criteria — when:** After the firm has been acquired and while the consultant is activating or already running.

# Systems — change packet 023 (Failure mode = stop spending, keep listening)

**Seat:** Systems Analyst.
**When:** 2026-08-21 09:50 UTC.
**What this is:** the cut for the failure mode that has been open since 2026-08-15 16:58. Implementer **only implements**.
**Why:** Founder: *“the failure mode is simple — it just means we're not gonna waste resources trying to make that objective happen. But if it happens, if it clears, then of course it's still a win… the objective is met.”*
**Join:** 022 (objective met is a Local event) — **read 022 first; this packet depends on its detect-on-the-write path.** 010 `campaign_failure` · `cascade.ts` ladder · [`SYSTEMS-OBJECTIVE-ESCROW.md`](./SYSTEMS-OBJECTIVE-ESCROW.md) (direction; not built).
**Flag:** 15:43 untouched. Do not recut 015 / 019. **#108 merged.** Cut 022 first.
**UI:** none required.
**Instructions:** founder only.

---

## 1. The law, stated once

Failure is **not** an ending. It is a **spending decision**.

| | Outbound (resources we spend) | Inbound (completion we listen for) |
|---|---|---|
| **Pursuing** | sends, attempts, channel ladder, escalation | listening |
| **Exhausted (failure mode)** | **stops** | **still listening** |
| **Nullified** (escrow era — not this packet) | stopped | **stops. The door refuses.** |

Two lines, not one. Exhaustion closes only the **outbound**. The objective stays claimable: if it clears later on its own, *“it still counts.”* Only **nullification** closes the inbound — and the only thing that nullifies is the firm pulling their money, which is [`SYSTEMS-OBJECTIVE-ESCROW.md`](./SYSTEMS-OBJECTIVE-ESCROW.md) and is **not built now**.

This is why 022 had to come first. Once detection happens **on the completion write** instead of inside the tick's open-attempt loop, closing attempts no longer blinds us. Before 022, "stop spending" and "keep listening" were the same switch. Now they are two.

## 2. The bug this fixes

`cascade.ts` (~533): when the channel ladder has no forward channel (`!toChannel`), it records `campaign_failure` and dispatches the event — then leaves `active_attempts.status = 'open'`.

So the tick picks that attempt up again. And again. Every subsequent due window with no forward channel writes **another** `campaign_failure` row and **re-dispatches** the event. That is:

- exactly the resource waste the founder is describing, and
- a duplicate-event bug — a workflow subscribed to `campaign_failure` fires repeatedly for one failure.

## 3. Hard decisions

### 3.1 Exhaustion is terminal for the attempt

```sql
-- 'exhausted' joins the existing status vocabulary.
-- DO NOT reuse 'nullified' — see 3.4.
UPDATE active_attempts
   SET status = 'exhausted', updated_at = now(),
       state = state || jsonb_build_object('exhausted_at', now()::text,
                                           'campaign_failure_id', $2::text)
 WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'open';
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -e

JSON_MODE=false
DRY_RUN=false
ALLOW_EXISTING=false
SHORT_NAME=""
BRANCH_NUMBER=""
USE_TIMESTAMP=false
NUMBER_EXPLICIT=false
ARGS=()
i=1
while [ $i -le $# ]; do
    arg="${!i}"
    case "$arg" in
        --json)
            JSON_MODE=true
            ;;
        --dry-run)
            DRY_RUN=true
            ;;
        --allow-existing-branch)
            ALLOW_EXISTING=true
            ;;
        --short-name)
            if [ $((i + 1)) -gt $# ]; then
                echo 'Error: --short-name requires a value' >&2
                exit 1
            fi
            i=$((i + 1))
            next_arg="${!i}"
            # Check if the next argument is another option (starts with --)
            if [[ "$next_arg" == --* ]]; then
                echo 'Error: --short-name requires a value' >&2
                exit 1
            fi
            SHORT_NAME="$next_arg"
            ;;
        --number)

2. **IF EXISTS**: Load `.specify/memory/constitution.md` for project principles and governance constraints.

3. Load the current spec file. Perform a structured ambiguity & coverage scan using this taxonomy. For each category, mark status: Clear / Partial / Missing. Produce an internal coverage map used for prioritization (do not output raw map unless no questions will be asked).

   Functional Scope & Behavior:
   - Core user goals & success criteria
   - Explicit out-of-scope declarations
   - User roles / personas differentiation

   Domain & Data Model:
   - Entities, attributes, relationships
   - Identity & uniqueness rules
   - Lifecycle/state transitions
   - Data volume / scale assumptions

   Interaction & UX Flow:
   - Critical user journeys / sequences
   - Error/empty/loading states
   - Accessibility or localization notes

   Non-Functional Quality Attributes:
   - Performance (latency, throughput targets)
   - Scalability (horizontal/vertical, limits)
   - Reliability & availability (uptime, recovery expectations)
   - Observability (logging, metrics, tracing signals)
   - Security & privacy (authN/Z, data protection, threat assumptions)
   - Compliance / regulatory constraints (if any)

   Integration & External Dependencies:
   - External services/APIs and failure modes
   - Data import/export formats
   - Protocol/versioning assumptions

   Edge Cases & Failure Handling:
   - Negative scenarios
   - Rate limiting / throttling
   - Conflict resolution (e.g., concurrent edits)

   Constraints & Tradeoffs:
   - Technical constraints (language, storage, hosting)
   - Explicit tradeoffs or rejected alternatives

   Terminology & Consistency:
   - Canonical glossary terms
   - Avoided synonyms / deprecated terms

   Completion Signals:
   - Acceptance criteria testability
   - Measurable Definition of Done style indicators

   Misc / Placeholders:
   - TODO markers / unresolved decisions
   - Ambiguous adjectives ("robust", "intuitive") lacking quantification

   For each category with Partial or Missing status, add a candidate question opportunity unless:
   - Clarification would not materially change implementation or validation strategy
   - The item is specifically about implementation method, tech-stack comparison, or task breakdown (note internally)

4. Generate (internally) a prioritized queue of candidate clarification questions (maximum 5). Do NOT output them all at once. Apply these constraints:
    - Maximum of 5 total questions across the whole session.
    - Each question must be answerable with EITHER:
       - A short multiple‑choice selection (2–5 distinct, mutually exclusive options), OR
       - A one-word / short‑phrase answer (explicitly constrain: "Answer in <=5 words").
    - Only include questions whose answers materially impact architecture, data modeling, task decomposition, test design, UX behavior, operational readiness, or compliance validation.
    - Ensure category coverage balance: attempt to cover the highest impact unresolved categories first; avoid asking two low-impact questions when a single high-impact area (e.g., security posture) is unresolved.
    - Exclude questions already answered, trivial stylistic preferences, or plan-level execution details (unless blocking correctness).
    - Favor clarifications that reduce downstream rework risk or prevent misaligned acceptance tests.
    - If more than 5 categories remain unresolved, select the top 5 by (Impact * Uncertainty) heuristic.

5. Sequential questioning loop (interactive):
    - Present EXACTLY ONE question at a time.
    - **Question writing quality (applies to every question, MC or short-answer):**
       - Lead with `**Question:**` followed by a full interrogative that ends with `?`. The question text before the `?` must make sense on its own.
       - NEVER use a topic label, section heading, or requirement id as the question itself. For example, `Acceptance device/runtime matrix (FR-023)` is INVALID — it is a label, not a question.
       - After the `?`, the only permitted suffix is an optional parenthesized requirement/question id. Exact format: `**Question:** <interrogative>?` or `**Question:** <interrogative>? (FR-023)`. Never put the id before the `?`, and never use the id (alone or with a topic label) as the whole prompt.
       - Immediately after the question line, add one plain-language "Why it matters" sentence (the stake for acceptance or shipping) before the recommendation/options.
       - Use everyday wording; introduce jargon only if defined in the same sentence. Self-check: a reader who does not know Spec Kit must be able to answer from the Question line alone. Terse is fine; cryptic labels are not.
    - For multiple‑choice questions:
       - **Analyze all options** and determine the **most suitable option** based on:
          - Best practices for the project type
          - Common patterns in similar implementations
          - Risk reduction (security, performance, maintainability)
          - Alignment with any explicit project goals or constraints visible in the spec
       - Present your **recommended option prominently** at the top with clear reasoning (1-2 sentences explaining why this is the best choice).
       - Format as: `**Recommended:** Option [X] - <reasoning>`
       - Then render all options as a Markdown table:

       | Option | Description |
       |--------|-------------|
       | A | <Option A description> |
       | B | <Option B description> |
       | C | <Option C description> (add D/E as needed up to 5) |
       | Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) (Include only if free-form alternative is appropriate) |

       - After the table, add: `You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.`
    - For short‑answer style (no meaningful discrete options):
       - Provide your **suggested answer** based on best practices and context.
       - Format as: `**Suggested:** <your proposed answer> - <brief reasoning>`
       - Then output: `Format: Short answer (<=5 words). You can accept the suggestion by saying "yes" or "suggested", or provide your own answer.`
    - After the user answers:
       - If the user replies with "yes", "recommended", or "suggested", use your previously stated recommendation/suggestion as the answer.
       - Otherwise, validate the answer maps to one option or fits the <=5 word constraint.
       - If ambiguous, ask for a quick disambiguation (count still belongs to same question; do not advance).
       - Once satisfactory, record it in working memory (do not yet write to disk) and move to the next queued question.
    - Stop asking further questions when:
       - All critical ambiguities resolved early (remaining queued items become unnecessary), OR
       - User signals completion ("done", "good", "no more"), OR
       - You reach 5 asked questions.
    - Never reveal future queued questions in advance.
    - If no valid questions exist at start, immediately report no critical ambiguities.

6. Integration after EACH accepted answer (incremental update approach):
    - Maintain in-memory representation of the spec (loaded once at start) plus the raw file contents.
    - For the first integrated answer in this session:
       - Ensure a `## Clarifications` section exists (create it just after the highest-level contextual/overview section per the spec template if missing).
       - Under it, create (if not present) a `### Session YYYY-MM-DD` subheading for today.
    - Append a bullet line immediately after acceptance: `- Q: <question> → A: <final answer>`.
    - Then immediately apply the clarification to the most appropriate section(s):
       - Functional ambiguity → Update or add a bullet in Functional Requirements.
       - User interaction / actor distinction → Update User Stories or Actors subsection (if present) with clarified role, constraint, or scenario.
       - Data shape / entities → Update Data Model (add fields, types, relationships) preserving ordering; note added constraints succinctly.
       - Non-functional constraint → Add/modify measurable criteria in Success Criteria > Measurable Outcomes (convert vague adjective to metric or explicit target).
       - Edge case / negative flow → Add a new bullet under Edge Cases / Error Handling (or create such subsection if template provides placeholder for it).
       - Terminology conflict → Normalize term across spec; retain original only if necessary by adding `(formerly referred to as "X")` once.
    - If the clarification invalidates an earlier ambiguous statement, replace that statement instead of duplicating; leave no obsolete contradictory text.
    - Save the spec file AFTER each integration to minimize risk of context loss (atomic overwrite).
    - Preserve formatting: do not reorder unrelated sections; keep heading hierarchy intact.
    - Keep each inserted clarification minimal and testable (avoid narrative drift).

7. Validation (performed after EACH write plus final pass):
   - Clarifications session contains exactly one bullet per accepted answer (no duplicates).
   - Total asked (accepted) questions ≤ 5.
   - Updated sections contain no lingering vague placeholders the new answer was meant to resolve.
   - No contradictory earlier statement remains (scan for now-invalid alternative choices removed).
   - Markdown structure valid; only allowed new headings: `## Clarifications`, `### Session YYYY-MM-DD`.
   - Terminology consistency: same canonical term used across all updated sections.

8. Write the updated spec back to `FEATURE_SPEC`.

9. **Re-validate Spec Quality Checklist** (if it exists):
   - Check if `FEATURE_DIR/checklists/requirements.md` exists.
   - If it does NOT exist, skip this step silently.
   - If it exists:
     1. Read the checklist file.
     2. Identify all GitHub task-list checkbox lines — lines matching `- [ ]`, `- [x]`, or `- [X]` (case-insensitive, tolerant of leading whitespace for nested items) outside of code fences. Ignore all other content (headings, notes, non-checkbox bullets, metadata).
     3. For each checkbox line, record its current marker state (checked or unchecked) and item text into a before-snapshot list.
     4. Re-evaluate each checkbox item against the **updated** spec (the version just saved in step 7).
     5. For each checkbox item, update only if the checked/unchecked state actually changes:
        - If the item now passes and was unchecked: change `[ ]` to `[x]`.
        - If the item now fails and was checked: change `[x]`/`[X]` to `[ ]`.

**Refresh facts — secondary**
> As Engagement contact, I can answer one consolidated form for outstanding self-reportable facts,
> and reply when my situation changes.

**Silence — secondary**
> As Engagement contact, I can silence or opt out at any point.

**Book — secondary (closure hop)**
> As Engagement contact, I can book a meeting when invited and arrive where the firm already knows my
> current facts — so that the Consultant takes the meeting with a live brief.

---

## C. Operator — house-global surfaces

*Subject is the Operator throughout. What the engine does under these is requirement, surfaced at
leaves — never restated here as the engine's outcome.*

**Acquisition & ads — secondary**
> As Operator, I can run the firm-acquisition Approach (feed → ad → capture, inside the click budget)
> and read who understood-but-didn't-tap versus didn't-understand — so that a captured firm can be
> staged for activation.

**Activation & forward-deploy — secondary** *(candidate co-core)*
> As Operator, I can stage a no-login prepared workspace for a captured firm from house templates and
> public facts, walk the firm through readiness, and secure its database authorization and escrow —
> so that the Consultant reaches a running desk.

**Reference data — secondary**
> As Operator, I can keep the immigration reference tables versioned and current as data, without a
> code deploy — so that house-authored evaluation packs score eligibility on today's rules.

**Configuration libraries — secondary**
> As Operator, I can author and version the evaluation packs, automation workflows, and engagement
> templates that run the product — so that a firm's operations can be bound from house-authored packs
> rather than built per firm.

**Oversight — secondary**
> As Operator, I can watch engagement and sequence health across every firm and drill into any one —
> so that a failing tenancy is caught before the Consultant loses meetings.

**Audit trail — secondary**
> As Operator, I can see who changed which operation, when, and on which firm — so that support and
> founder oversight can account for every change over real client books.

**Register & evolution — secondary** *(prototype-time house tooling only; no firm-facing surface)*
> As Operator, I can document friction from running firms and regenerate the methodology into house
> build tooling — so that the next authored operations reach the configuration libraries.

**Founder & agency controls — secondary**
> As Operator, I can set cross-firm bounds, kill-switches, and agency policy — so that many tenancies
> are overseen without leaking controls into any firm's workspace.

---

## D. Operator — per-tenancy admin surfaces

**Provision (assisted door) — secondary**
> As Operator, I can provision a firm and its user through the assisted door — so that the Consultant
> reaches the same desk when ALG isn't the path.

**Commercial (escrow / contingent terms) — secondary**
> As Operator, I can hold and oversee a firm's escrow and contingent terms — so that the Consultant
> can accept the terms and reach running.

**Firm operations bind — secondary**
> As Operator, I can bind house-authored evaluation, automation, and campaign packs under a firm's
> identity — so that the Consultant's book is worked without the firm authoring anything.

**Book readiness — secondary**
> As Operator, I can run the reachability gate over a firm's book — so that only reachable contacts
> enter engagement.

**Firm health — secondary**
> As Operator, I can see engagement health scoped to one firm — so that support can restore it and
> the Consultant keeps getting meetings.

**Activation state — secondary**
> As Operator, I can see a firm's forward-deploy and hard-input progress toward running — so that a
> stalled firm is moved to a running desk.

---

## E. Operator — customer support / success

**Keep the firm running — secondary**
> As Operator, I can answer a running firm's questions and work its tickets with that firm's bind,
> health, and commercial context — so that the Consultant's firm keeps running.

Consultant core → Engagement contact (arrives re-engaged) → Book → Consultant takes the meeting.

+
+1. Specified and clear → the requirement stands.
+2. Specified but not clear (packet incomplete, or store/control not ascribed) → list it and why. Do not invent the missing grain.
+
+Rationale: Engineer two-bucket law; Story under-claim posture; Decision constitution against catch-all deferral.
+
+### V. Write-Set Is The Shape After A Node
+After a node finishes, the next step MUST have every write that run made. The next node picks which of those writes it is about. A field catalog MUST NOT be hard-coded in the client. Hearing a completion as a trigger on a different automation is a second door; it MUST NOT substitute for the handle on the same canvas.
+
+Click the node = configure. Palette **Switch** is the many-path node. Node-menu **Switch** means change this Trigger/Action’s kind. Those words MUST NOT be mixed. Teaching copy and captions on plates are not nodes.
+
+Rationale: Automations face law 33; Primitives; IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT; A26 vs If/Switch packet.
+
+## Product Boundaries And Honesty
+
+Tower is an always-on immigration-consultancy workspace run by Om Coda as an **agency product**, not a self-serve tool each firm configures alone. The consultant’s north-star outcome is: hand over the private book, authorize it to work under the firm license, and receive eligible clients booked — without authoring engagement. Operator / house configuration libraries author evaluation, automations, and sequences; per-tenancy admin **binds** those packs under a firm identity.
+
+Engagement phases are Opt-in → Re-engagement (nudges) → Reactivation. Engine 2 motion law: reactivation first if anything is reactivation-worthy; nudge only otherwise; one nudge consolidates every outstanding self-reportable need into a single form; when reactivation fires, secondary signals ride as agenda on the live brief; **one client, one motion, ever**. Attempt / channel-ownership is a separate engine inside one sequence.
+
+Hard human gates MUST NOT be automated away: seed capture; assisted provision and OTP verify; database authorization; escrow accept; client opt-in / not silenced; meeting booking; firm responsibility to refuse illegal or unethical outreach.
+
+End-clients pay Tower nothing. Escrow is firm↔Om Coda contingent terms; Tower MUST NOT hold immigrant settlement funds. Public-before-contact detection of end-client eligibility is out of product. Cold email is not V1 Approach. Meta acquisition, Register/evolution as firm-facing product, and escrow fulfillment remain deferred or prototype-honest where the snapshot says so.
+
+Send paths MUST respect consent, halt, and silence. Unprovisioned OTP requests MUST return generic success and issue no code (anti-enumeration).
+
+## Specification And Verification
+
+Locked plates are read with five buckets: Copy; Do not build; Implied; Completes; Out of scope this build. Captions on images are not spec.
+
+Verification in this repository is **manual** on the running SPA at `/prototype-ant` (distinct screens) plus `npm run build`. There is no ESLint / Prettier / Vitest / Jest / Playwright / `tsc` gate. That absence is repository fact, not a quality claim that automated tests exist.
+
+This constitution governs later Spec Kit planning and analysis. Unrealistic rules MUST NOT be invented merely to fill the template. Test-first automated TDD is **not** a standing Tower law in the snapshot and MUST NOT be asserted here.
+

# Magic / direct access link

**Date:** 2026-08-11  
**Status:** shipped on this branch — closes gap A in `APP-ELEVATION-GAP.md`

## Product intent

Invite is a **direct access URL**, not a login portal as the product.

- Open `/a/<token>` → one-time redeem → session cookie → `/prototype-ant`
- OTP `/login` remains as fallback

## Shape

| Piece | Path |
|-------|------|
| Table | `access_links` (`008_access_links.sql`) |
| Redeem | `POST /auth/access/redeem` `{ token }` → sets `tower_session` |
| Issue (auth) | `POST /auth/access/issue` — admin / self / `x-access-issue-secret` |
| Issue (wire) | `POST /wire/machine/access-invite` — mint + email from Provision |
| Provision | Returns `accessPath` (= `loginPath` when mint succeeds) |
| SPA entry | `/a/:token` → `AccessEntry` |

## TTL / consume

- 7 days (`ACCESS_LINK_TTL_MS`)
- One active link per user; re-issue invalidates prior
- Single-use: `consumed_at` on redeem

## Ops

```bash
npm run db:migrate   # applies 008_access_links.sql
npm run issue:access -- user@firm.com
npm run verify:access
```

Optional env:

- `PUBLIC_APP_URL` / `APP_ORIGIN` — absolute URL in invite emails

# FIRM-BINDING

**Branch:** `cursor/firm-binding-6565`  
**Date:** 2026-08-10  
**Deferred (untouched):** Escrow · Meta  

**Done bar:** Provision a firm in the app → log in as that consultant → land in that firm’s empty book → upload a list → operator designs/binds the sequence → outreach fires for **that** firm — proven on the real wire with a firm I created, not the demo tenant.

---

## What changed (binding, not just isolation)

| Before | After |
|--------|--------|
| Provision wrote TEXT `firm-*` into CT and a **different** UUID into auth | **One UUID** written to `firms` + `ct_firms` + `campaign_states` + `users` |
| Login session firm ≠ machine firm | Session `firm_id` **is** the provisioned firm |
| Consultant Contacts showed demo Cedar list | Contacts load `contact_records` for the **session** firm (empty when fresh) |
| `machineApi` / halt / CRM grant stamped demo firm | Session firm via `getActiveFirmId` / wire cookie |
| OTP verify returned `{ok:true}` only | Returns `user.firmId`; Login calls `setActiveFirmId` + `refresh()` |
| Auth-disabled always overwrote with `VITE_DEV_FIRM_ID` | Real session cookie **wins** over bypass |

---

## Grep — session/machine path

```text
rg 'firm-cedar' server/wire-service/machine.ts src/app/wire/reals/machineApi.ts
# (no matches)

rg 'const FIRM' src/app/wire/standins/machineApi.ts
# (no const FIRM = "firm-cedar")
```

**Remain as seed/demo labels only:** `demoIds.ts` (`CT_DEMO`), operator `DEMO_FIRMS` chrome, seeds, verify scripts targeting the Cedar seed tenant.

---

## Six-step walk (self-provisioned firm) — Postgres proof

`npm run verify:firm-binding` against Session-pooler — **PASSED**

# Operator — Configuration libraries

**Kind:** secondary  
**Subject:** Operator (house-global)

**Statement**
> As Operator, I can author and version the evaluation packs, automation workflows, and engagement
> templates that run the product — so that a firm's operations can be bound from house-authored packs
> rather than built per firm.

**Note:** This is where engagement / eligibility **authorship** lives. Execution after bind is
requirement at leaves — not a Consultant outcome. Hub Automations / Agents today are
**existing-wrong-seat**; rightful Module is Configuration libraries (operator).  
**Affordance rule:** Every Clarity names the control. Publishing here does **not** bind a firm — Firm operations bind dropdowns consume published versions later.

---

## Root — outcome

**Clarity:** *(statement)*  
**Criteria — when:** Continuously as methodology and rules evolve.  
**Conditions:** House authors; firms do not; open-box without code deploy for ops tweaks.

---

## Depth 1 — first How

**Q:** How do I author and version the evaluation packs, automation workflows, and engagement templates that run the product?

**Clarity:** Starting from Configuration libraries, click **Evaluation packs**, **Automation workflows**, or **Engagement templates** in the Libraries nav (left list). On the chosen catalog, click a row (or **New**), edit in the editor/canvas, then click **Publish version** (primary button) — so firms can later pick that version in Firm operations bind dropdowns. No firm picker exists on this module.

**DNA for children:**
1. author Evaluation packs
2. author Automation workflows
3. author Engagement templates

---
